title: The Survey
description: Nine sheets of good paper in an unlocked rack, and every fact you have collected this year written down on them in one hand, in order, with a total at the bottom.

the_rack.title: Not in the strongbox
the_rack.objective: The strongbox holds the wages; the rack holds the working paper. To inspect it, return to Rourke in his office and ask what's in the rack.
the_rack.journal: Rourke's strongbox is bolted through the floor and joist, with eleven pounds inside. The rolled paper beside it is unlocked. Nobody at the works thinks it's worth anything. It's only the survey.

in_hand.title: In hand
in_hand.objective: You have it. Decide what to do with it: take it to Ludo Corse at the Factor's House in Greyhythe, or to Alder Pyke on Granary Row.
in_hand.journal: The survey covers every field, road, weir, seam and roof between the ford and Greyhythe, measured and valued in one hand. Rivermark is on sheet six. It isn't drawn as a town, but entered in the margin under "clearance", as a cost. The figure has been revised downward twice. Someone sat down twice and decided we'd cost less than that.

took_the_survey.title: Kept
took_the_survey.journal: I have the survey: nine sheets, rolled and tied under my arm, with Rivermark entered as a cost on sheet six. Nobody has tried to take it. A document is worth what its holder can do with it. I'm still working that out, and I'm not sure I was right to keep it.

burned_the_survey.title: Burned
burned_the_survey.journal: Three years of chain-work, nine sheets, and about four hundred days' wages, gone as quickly as paper burns. They'll survey it again; that will take three years. For that long, nobody will know this valley's worth, including us. Someone will start asking who stood by the fire.

sold_it_back.title: Sold back
sold_it_back.journal: Five hundred gold, counted out without argument, and retainer articles at forty a quarter for services left unspecified. He had them ready before I came. Not for me, but for whoever came. I keep thinking of the chair, worn through at the arms, and the paper, already drawn.

warned_the_town.title: Read out on Granary Row
warned_the_town.journal: Pyke read the survey aloud; he can read one, and I can't. His chain measured half of it. Forty people stood in the rain on Granary Row as he told them what their roofs were valued at. Reed wrote it all down. No law is broken, and nobody can be arrested. The town knows what's coming. That's all knowing can do, and Pyke is out of work.
